source.title: Simply reverse engineering gpt2-small (Layer 0, Part 1: Attention)

record.file_problem: Whole post and comments are present.
record.tranche_reason: The post analyzes GPT2-small’s embedding geometry and performs embedding-weight ablations, providing a different kind of evidence about feature distribution in an LLM. It does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The author explicitly contrasts GPT2-small’s large, non-sparse modules and linear embedding structure with atomic sparse features compressed into superposition. The post does not test toy-model superposition, SAE feature recovery, polysemanticity, or the dimensionality of superposed features. Loss trends across cutoffs are described in text but their exact values are available only in figures.
record.test_reason: This is a hand reverse-engineering of GPT2-small layer 0: embedding geometry, a split into token and position subspaces, and attention-head functions. It never measures whether features are superposed, spread across many neurons, or recoverable by a dictionary. Its anti-superposition remark is an interpretive aside drawn from word-analogy structure, not a test. Linear analogy structure is also compatible with superposed linear directions, so it cannot separate the versions. The token/position split and the neuron-aligned positional code are related but different constructs, recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The author concludes that GPT2-small's first residual stream splits into large, non-sparse, minimally interacting position and token modules. Layer-0 attention heads then fall into four archetypes (word completion, same-token, context clarification, head 9 'scope finding'). Modular manual analysis of layer 0 is described as not particularly difficult. The superposition remark is a passing interpretive claim, not the main conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: Manual analysis of GPT2-small embeddings and attention weights, plus neuron-mask loss tests; not the original toy-network feature optimization or sparsity sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: The loss trend depends on the cutoff; the author reports a small exception near the start of the token-side cutoff sweep. The approximately 30-neuron token-mask result leaves the unembedding unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: Positional embedding information is neuron-aligned and highly redundant: linear and periodic piecewise-linear curves sit in about 55 neurons, mostly orthogonal to the dominant token-embedding directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned positional embeddings in GPT2-small occupy a dedicated, neuron-aligned subspace separate from token semantics, rather than being superposed with token features.

fits_no_version.finding: The token embedding shows linear analogy structure and linear 'general knowledge' (country to politician) by vector arithmetic.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT2-small's token embedding encodes semantic relations linearly.

fits_no_version.finding: The author argues the key-position slope used by attention heads is a functionally important 'feature' that is not expressible as a direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some computationally relevant structures are not representable as activation-space directions.

record.problems: The feature-distribution evidence is interpretive and focused on GPT2-small’s embeddings and early residual stream. Several loss results are shown only in figures, with no exact values or uncertainty estimates stated in the text. The author notes that the linearized layernorm approximation ignores lateral inhibition and is imperfect.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. Other reported attention-head analyses concern attention patterns and head functions rather than the listed feature-superposition versions.

untested.parts: No toy model, sparsity sweep or feature geometry.
No measure of features spread across neurons and no dictionary or SAE recovery. The anti-superposition claim is asserted, not tested.
The author argues the key-position slope is not a direction, but this is not about what is superposed and is not tested against multi-dimensional superposed features.

record.verdict_notes: The reader over-linked all rows to V4 and labelled it 'supports'. Yet the author's own stance is against superposition, and none of the measures bear on superposition. This is a LessWrong post with no controls or uncertainty estimates; the layernorm is linearised, which ignores lateral inhibition.

versions.untested_parts: No toy network with more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transition, or regular superposition geometry is tested.
No test of polysemantic neurons, feature competition for capacity, or important features receiving dedicated dimensions.
No test of polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The analysis concerns GPT2-small’s token and position embeddings and early residual stream, not feature distributions throughout LLM activations or SAE-recovered features.
No SAE features or tests of their completeness, stability, or canonical status.
The post discusses a key-position slope that is not usefully described as a direction, but does not test whether superposed features are 1-D directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.size_stated: 768 residual-stream neurons; token embedding is 50257 x 768
rows.operation_detail: Analyzed token embeddings and their semantic relationships in the residual-stream representation.
rows.measure: Semantic relationships in the token embedding; the author describes semantic information as part of its linear structure and says the representation is not composed only of atomic sparse features compressed into superposition.
rows.value: The author reports that for each of several countries, a contemporary politician from that country appears within the top 5; Merkel is 32nd for a Germany-related query without an added who/person boost.
rows.note: This is evidence about GPT2-small’s token embedding, not a direct census of abstract features across model activations.
rows.check: Word-analogy and nearest-token rankings in the token embedding test linear semantic structure, not superposition. Neither superposed nor non-superposed features would be ruled out by them. The 'top 5' and 'Merkel 32nd' values are qualitative retrieval anecdotes with no baseline.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Compared neurons ranked by positional importance with token-embedding directions from an SVD.
rows.measure: Overlap between positionally important neurons and directions important to the token embedding.
rows.value: The roughly 50 most positionally important neurons project almost exclusively onto roughly the 100 least important token-embedding directions; positional information falls off quickly after neuron 50, with practically none past 100.
rows.locator: The word embedding and position embedding are mostly separate
rows.note: The post interprets this as the network keeping token and position embeddings mostly separate; it is not an SAE or abstract-feature analysis.
rows.check: Overlap between positional neurons and SVD token directions measures subspace separation of two embeddings. It is not a measure of features distributed across neurons in the V4 sense. No baseline is given.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Set selected embedding weights to zero according to a cutoff in neurons ranked by positional importance.

conditions.value: sweep over neuron cutoffs; exact values not stated in text
remove token-embedding weights after/before the cutoff, position-embedding weights after/before the cutoff, or both, as described

rows.measure: Loss change under token-side, position-side, and combined embedding masks.
rows.value: The text says position-side loss decreases with larger cutoff and is nearly equal to unpatched loss from neuron 60 onward; token-side loss increases with larger cutoff, with a small exception at the start; the combined patch gives a loss difference close to the sum of the individual differences.
rows.note: The trends are described in text, but exact plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The masking loss sweep tests how separable the token and position subspaces are, not superposition. Values appear only in a figure.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Removed token data from the approximately 30 most positionally important neurons by setting embedding weights to zero, without changing the unembedding.
rows.note: The author attributes this result to an architectural asymmetry introduced by patching the embedding but not the tied unembedding. It shows a small overlap can be beneficial to remove under this intervention, not a general feature-capacity effect.
rows.check: The loss decrease is attributed by the author to untying embedding and unembedding, an architectural artefact. No magnitude is stated, and it has no bearing on any version.

rows.subject: gpt2-small
rows.operation_detail: Summarized the inferred allocation of residual-stream neurons to token and position information.
rows.measure: Inferred neuron allocation between position and token information.
rows.value: Approximately 55 neurons dedicated to position data, approximately 40 with minimal position data and some token data, and approximately 670 carrying token data.
rows.note: These are the author’s approximate interpretation of the embedding analyses, not a direct count of learned abstract features.
rows.check: The ~55/~40/~670 neuron allocation is the author's approximate summary of R2 and R3, not an independent measurement. It concerns token versus position subspaces, not feature superposition.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: GPT2-small token and position embedding analysis
reader_labels.reason: The post reports linear semantic structure in the token embedding and an inferred broad allocation of residual-stream neurons to token information, consistent with indirect evidence of distributed representations in this setting (R1, R2, R5). The evidence is limited to the analyzed embeddings and early residual stream.
